name: Lena Düpont - Proposition de la Commission
title: REPORT on the draft for a Council directive amending Directive (EU) 2015/637 on the coordination and cooperation measures to facilitate consular protection for unrepresented citizens of the Union in third countries and Directive (EU) 2019/997 establishing an EU Emergency Travel Document
part_text:
The European Parliament wants to make it easier for European Union citizens abroad to get help from another member country's embassy when their own country has none nearby. It says citizens should count as "unrepresented" if they cannot safely reach their own embassy within 48 hours, or sooner in danger. It also asks for more crisis drills, better warnings and travel advice, more money and staff for the European Union's diplomatic service, and clearer rules on personal data.

- **What changes:** a 48-hour rule for who counts as unrepresented, yearly crisis drills, and better alerts and travel advice.
- **Who it affects:** European Union citizens living or travelling outside the Union, and member countries' embassies.
- **What happens next:** the Parliament approves the draft with changes and asks the Council of the European Union to accept them.
